prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission; ground segment plans, acquires, operates, produces, archives, controls access (excludes spacecraft, launch, user processing). Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing policy; contact = readiness check, monitoring, post-pass closure; sends constraints to Mission Planning System (MPS), receives command preparation package. Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT): console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on telemetry mismatch; uses Antenna Deicing Notice; receives maneuver recommendation package above conjunction threshold. Escalation console>discipline lead>mission management. Possible fault: preserve command state, no discretionary commanding. Stack queued only with MCC+SOT concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): shall validate stacks (syntax, timing, ranges, sequencing, mode, schedule, burn plan); shall reject unapproved edits, missing provenance, expired config, out-of-window; consults Telemetry Ingest Service, Orbit Determination Engine (produces Laser Retroreflector Window). Cybersecurity Desk reviews exceptions; receives Security Exception Ticket from Ground Network Manager (Juniper). Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): sends Star Tracker Mask File; ephemerides to MCC, MPS, PPF (shall include validity, frame, generation time, use statement); publishes orbit quality changes to archive operations queue before catalogue validity flags update. Flight Dynamics Team: uses Doppler Residual Report, produces Ephemeris Delta Note. Network Control System (Lantern): routing, station allocation; sends MCC antenna status, link config; uses Security Exception Ticket; shall keep last validated routing, reject unreviewed changes during transfers. Payload Calibration Team: produces Calibration Patch Bundle; may request reprocessing for systematic issues. Product Quality Service (PQS): uses patch bundle; sets quality flags/public status; produces Product Hold List. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): Primary and Backup Processing Clusters; both down: suspend; recovery: latency-committed products first, then acquisition order. Long Term Archive (Granite): authoritative repository; admits only after PPF delivers package, quality metadata, checksums; persistent IDs; sends Storage Watermark Snapshot daily; publishes catalogue to User Services Portal after PQS status and embargo check; raw kept mission life plus post-mission; deletion only per approved rules. User Services Portal: search, preview, order, resumable rate-limited download; scoped authorization; anonymous only for approved open classes.

New part:
S195: Product Quality Service records the reason for any reprocessing decision so that users can distinguish scientific updates from operational recovery actions.
S196: During reprocessing, Long Term Archive preserves the replaced product version unless the applicable policy allows consolidation after a defined comparison period.
S197: Catalogue records show processing baseline, sensing time, publication time, quality status, and replacement relationships for each released product.
S198: Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Pass Replay Packet to confirm that archived downlink context can support anomaly reconstruction.
S199: External interfaces expose catalogue search, subscription notification, product ordering, and download status using versioned service contracts.
S200: Cybersecurity Desk reviews public interface changes before deployment to confirm authentication, logging, and abuse-control requirements are satisfied.
S201: If Long Term Archive cannot meet a restore or publication commitment, User Services Portal displays a service status message and operations staff open the normal incident process.
S202: Security operations for the Sentinel Vale ground segment are based on least privilege, strong authentication, network segmentation, and continuous audit collection across all operational environments.
S203: Mission Control Center maintains the authority boundary for routine spacecraft operations and confirms that elevated access is tied to an approved shift role and a time-limited operational need.
S204: Cybersecurity Desk reviews privileged access daily and challenges dormant, shared, or unexplained accounts before they can be used during a pass or processing shift.
S205: Network Control System enforces approved routing paths between ground stations, processing services, and external interfaces, and it records configuration changes in the operational log.
S206: Command Validation Gateway accepts the mask file only when the integrity check, configuration identifier, and operator approval state match the active security baseline.
S207: Mission Planning System treats the retroreflector window as a constrained planning input and prevents its use outside the approved scheduling interval.
S208: An anomaly is first classified by impact to safety, command authority, data custody, service continuity, and user-facing commitments.
S209: Spacecraft Operations Team leads triage for spacecraft safety indicators, while Ground Network Manager leads triage for antenna, link, and site-service indicators.
S210: Flight Dynamics Team assesses orbit and timing effects when tracking quality, contact geometry, or prediction freshness is suspected to be degraded.
S211: Payload Calibration Team assesses product integrity when calibration state, instrument configuration, or processing repeatability is questioned.
S212: Cybersecurity Desk assumes coordination authority when the anomaly includes suspicious authentication, unexpected data movement, unexplained service behavior, or evidence of tampering.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
